transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in today?

Hi, Doctor. Thank you for seeing me. Um, well, occupational health at the department actually sent me in. They... they seem to think I'm not eating enough, which, honestly, I think is a bit of an overreaction. 

I'm really just trying to stay disciplined. Most days I just keep it to black coffee while I'm on shift... maybe a plain yogurt. And then, you know, just a few bites of chicken at night. It's just that if I sit down and eat a full meal, it... it feels like I'm letting my standards slip. I have to stay sharp for the job, you know? 

Does that make sense? I hope I'm answering your question okay.
Do you find yourself very worried about gaining weight or do you go out of your way to avoid gaining weight, even if others say you're already underweight?

Well, I... I wouldn't say I'm panicked about it, exactly. I just want to stay fit for duty, you know? But, um... I guess I do keep a pretty strict eye on things. 

To be completely honest with you, if the scale is up even half a pound, I... I get this jolt. It just feels like I've completely lost control. And I'll usually spend the rest of the day cutting back a bit harder because I just... I really can't stand the idea of putting weight back on. 

I hope that doesn't sound too unreasonable? I'm just trying to be thorough for you. Am I answering that the way you need me to?
Do you feel that your weight or body shape has a strong impact on how you see yourself or how you feel about yourself overall?

Um, well... I don't want to sound superficial or anything. I know a guy my age shouldn't be obsessing over the mirror, but... I guess it does have an impact. 

To be honest with you, when I look in the mirror, I really don't see what occupational health or the other guys say they see. They keep saying I'm wasting away, but my eyes just go straight to my stomach and my waist. And if I don't look lean enough, I just... I find it really hard to respect myself. I kind of judge my whole day, my whole worth for the day, on whether I look disciplined enough in those areas. 

I hope it's okay to admit that to you... I know it probably sounds a bit foolish for a grown man to say. Is that the kind of thing you were asking about? I just want to make sure I'm giving you what you need.
Do you ever engage in behaviors like excessive exercise, fasting, or making yourself sick after eating in order to control your weight or shape?

Um, no, no I don't... I mean, I definitely don't make myself sick or anything like that. That's, um, that's not something I'd ever do. 

I do try to stay active, obviously, with the job and all. I might, you know, put in some extra miles on the treadmill or do some extra drills if I feel like I've slipped up a bit with my eating, but... I wouldn't call it excessive. It's just staying in shape for the uniform, really. And as for fasting... well, like I said, I keep things pretty light during the day, but I wouldn't call it a fast. Just, you know, being careful. 

I hope that's the right answer... I mean, I hope that makes sense. I'm really trying to be completely transparent with you here. Does that help clarify things?
Have these thoughts or behaviors around eating and body image been causing you a lot of distress or affecting your work, relationships, or other important areas of your life?

Well, I... I wouldn't say it's causing me a lot of distress, exactly. I mean, I try to handle things quietly, you know? But, um... I guess it has started to bleed into things a little bit. 

To be completely honest, occupational health has... well, they've held up my clearance for some of my field duties. It's frustrating because I feel fine, but I can tell the guys on the team are starting to second-guess if I'm fit to be out there with them. And, um, socially... I guess I have pulled back a bit. I stopped meeting people for lunch or dinner because I just... I really don't want to deal with the questions or the pressure about what's on my plate. It's just easier to eat alone. 

I hope that doesn't make me sound completely antisocial or anything. I'm just trying to keep my head down and do my job. Is that the kind of thing you were looking for? I want to make sure I'm giving you the full picture.
When you look at yourself in the mirror or think about your body, do you feel like you see yourself as bigger or heavier than you actually are?

Um... I'm not entirely sure how to answer that one, to be perfectly honest. I don't... I don't really think I see myself as bigger or heavier than I actually am. I mean, I don't feel like my eyes are playing tricks on me or anything like that. 

When I look in the mirror, I just see what's there. I see the, you know, the softness around my stomach that I still need to work on. I know the folks at work say I'm too light, but... I just see a guy who needs to keep his discipline up. I don't know if that means I'm seeing things wrong, or if I just have different standards for myself. 

I hope that's an okay answer? I'm really not trying to be difficult or evade the question, I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right information. Does that make sense at all?

latest_inference.note: The patient does not report significant distress or impairment in functioning directly from the eating behaviors themselves, but there is evidence of body image disturbance (judging self-worth based on body shape, preoccupation with perceived 'softness' despite being underweight), restrictive eating, and impact on social and occupational functioning. The patient also does not meet criteria for anorexia nervosa due to absence of marked weight loss or fear of gaining weight per se, which supports F50.01 (Atypical Anorexia Nervosa) over F50.00. No features of bulimia or binge eating, so F50.89 is ruled out.
